taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT. 

To convert this to your local time in Madrid:
1. **Identify the time zones for the deadline date:** In 2026, Daylight Saving Time in Spain (CEST to CET) ends on Sunday, October 25. Therefore, on October 30, Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET), which is **UTC+1**. In the US, Daylight Saving Time (PDT to PST) ends on Sunday, November 1. Therefore, on October 30, the Pacific time zone will still be on Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is **UTC-7**.
2. **Calculate the time difference:** The difference between UTC+1 and UTC-7 is 8 hours. Madrid is 8 hours ahead of PT.
3. **Add the offset to the deadline:** 11:59 PM on Friday, October 30, plus 8 hours results in 07:59 AM on the following day, Saturday, October 31.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is Monday, November 2, 2026. 

To determine your local time in Madrid:
1. **Identify the date:** Since "today" is Friday, October 30, 2026, "this coming Monday" is November 2, 2026.
2. **Determine the timezones:** 
   - In Spain, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). Therefore, on November 2, Madrid will be on **CET (UTC+1)**.
   - In the US, Daylight Saving Time ends on the first Sunday of November (November 1, 2026). Therefore, on November 2, Los Angeles will be on **PST (UTC-8)**.
3. **Calculate the difference:** The time difference between UTC+1 and UTC-8 is 9 hours.
4. **Convert the time:** 10:00 AM + 9 hours = 19:00.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00 Madrid time. In Spain, Daylight Saving Time (CEST, UTC+2) ends on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25.

At 03:00 AM on Sunday, October 25, the clocks will move back one hour to 02:00 AM (transitioning from CEST to CET, UTC+1).

1.  **Start Time:** Oct 24, 18:00 (UTC+2).
2.  **Duration:** 48 hours.
3.  **Elapsed time calculation:**
    *   From Oct 24, 18:00 to Oct 25, 03:00 (CEST) is 9 hours.
    *   At 03:00, the clock turns back to 02:00 (CET).
    *   From Oct 25, 02:00 (CET) to Oct 25, 18:00 (CET) is 16 hours.
    *   Total elapsed hours at Oct 25, 18:00 local time: 9 + 16 = 25 hours.
    *   Remaining hours needed: 48 - 25 = 23 hours.
    *   Oct 25, 18:00 + 23 hours = Oct 26, 17:00.

Alternatively, using UTC:
1.  **Start Time (UTC):** Oct 24, 16:00 UTC (18:00 - 2).
2.  **End Time (UTC):** Oct 24, 16:00 + 48 hours = Oct 26, 16:00 UTC.
3.  **Convert back to Madrid (UTC+1):** Oct 26, 16:00 + 1 = 17:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest begins on October 26, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT. In 2026, Daylight Saving Time in Spain ends on Sunday, October 25, meaning that on October 26, Madrid will have already transitioned to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1). Meanwhile, Daylight Saving Time in the US does not end until November 1, 2026, so Pacific Time will still be in Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7).

1.  **Calculate the deadline in PT:** 72 hours after October 26, 10:00 AM PT is October 29, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT.
2.  **Determine the time difference:** On October 29, Madrid is at UTC+1 and PT is at UTC-7. The difference is 8 hours.
3.  **Convert to Madrid time:** 10:00 AM + 8 hours = 18:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the result announcement time in Madrid, we first establish the deadline in UTC and then add the 36-hour duration.

1.  **Identify the Deadline in UTC:**
    *   The deadline is October 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET.
    *   In the United States, Daylight Saving Time (EDT, UTC-4) ends on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, this is November 1.
    *   Therefore, on October 31, ET is in **EDT (UTC-4)**.
    *   To convert 11:59 PM (23:59) EDT to UTC: $23:59 + 4 \text{ hours} = 03:59$ on **November 1, 2026 (UTC)**.

2.  **Add 36 Hours to the UTC Deadline:**
    *   03:59 on November 1, 2026 + 36 hours:
    *   $03:59 + 24 \text{ hours} = 03:59$ on November 2.
    *   $03:59 + 12 \text{ hours} = 15:59$ on **November 2, 2026 (UTC)**.

3.  **Convert the UTC Result Time to Madrid Local Time:**
    *   Madrid, Spain, follows Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) until the last Sunday of October.
    *   In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25.
    *   Therefore, by November 2, Madrid has switched to **CET (UTC+1)**.
    *   To convert 15:59 UTC to Madrid time: $15:59 + 1 \text{ hour} = 16:59$.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the Unix timestamp **1791788340** to your local time in Tokyo:

1.  **Convert the timestamp to UTC:**
    The Unix timestamp 1791788340 represents the number of seconds since the epoch (January 1, 1970).
    *   $1791788340 \div 86400$ (seconds per day) $\approx 20738.29$ days.
    *   $20738$ days from the epoch corresponds to **October 11, 2026**.
    *   The remainder $0.29097... \times 86400$ seconds is $25140$ seconds.
    *   $25140$ seconds is exactly **06:59:00**.
    *   So, the UTC time is **2026-10-11 06:59**.

2.  **Convert UTC to Tokyo Time (JST):**
    Tokyo is in Japan Standard Time (JST), which is **UTC+9**.
    *   $06:59 + 9$ hours = **15:59**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-11 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is provided in UTC (indicated by the "Z"). In Madrid, Spain, the transition from Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) occurs on the last Sunday of October. 

In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25th. The time change occurs at 01:00 UTC, when the local clocks move back from 03:00 CEST to 02:00 CET. Since the deadline is 02:30 UTC, it falls after this transition. Therefore, the offset is UTC+1.

02:30 + 1 hour = 03:30.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find your local deadline, we first determine the specific date and time mentioned:

1.  **Identify the last Sunday of October 2026:** October 1, 2026, is a Thursday. The Sundays in October 2026 are the 4th, 11th, 18th, and 25th. Therefore, the last Sunday is **October 25, 2026**.
2.  **Identify the Pacific Time (PT) offset:** In October, the US is in Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is **UTC-7**. The deadline is October 25, 2026, at 23:59 (11:59 PM) PDT.
3.  **Convert to UTC:** 23:59 on October 25 (UTC-7) is **06:59 on October 26 (UTC)**.
4.  **Identify Madrid's local time and offset:** In Spain, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October. On October 25, 2026, at 3:00 AM, Madrid will switch from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (**UTC+1**). 
5.  **Calculate Madrid time:** Since the deadline occurs on the morning of Monday, October 26, Madrid will be in Central European Time (UTC+1). Adding 1 hour to the UTC time (06:59) results in **07:59**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In the United States, Daylight Saving Time (DST) ends on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, the first Sunday of November is November 1st.

On that day, the US transitions from Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4) to Eastern Standard Time (EST, UTC-5) at 2:00 AM. Since the deadline is 12:00 noon, the transition will have already occurred, meaning the deadline is 12:00 PM EST (UTC-5).

Lima, Peru, operates on Peru Time (PET), which is permanently UTC-5. Since both the deadline (12:00 PM EST) and Lima time (PET) are UTC-5, the times are identical.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

"AoE" stands for "Anywhere on Earth," which refers to the time zone UTC-12. Tokyo, Japan, is in the Japan Standard Time (JST) zone, which is UTC+9.

To find the difference:
(UTC+9) - (UTC-12) = 21 hours.

Tokyo is 21 hours ahead of AoE. 

Adding 21 hours to December 31, 2026, at 24:00 (which is functionally January 1, 2027, at 00:00):
January 1, 2027, 00:00 + 21 hours = January 1, 2027, 21:00.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 5, 2026, Sydney will be observing Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT), which is UTC+11 (Daylight Saving begins on October 4, 2026). New York will be observing Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. 

The time difference is 15 hours (Sydney is 15 hours ahead of New York). Subtracting 15 hours from 5:00 PM (17:00) on October 5th results in 2:00 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
